options.text: a larger pretrained foundation model
a prompt engineering guide for employees
a fine-tuned language model trained on company documents
a grounding solution that retrieves approved content at query time

questions.stem:
Your company plans to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot to 200 employees. 
A company security policy requires that access to Microsoft 365 services be limited to compliant devices and protected by strong authentication controls.

You need to ensure that Copilot access meets the requirements.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Enforce Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies.
Increase the maximum token limit for Copilot responses.
Enable multifactor authentication (MFA) for all Copilot users.
Move Microsoft 365 Apps to the Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel.
Use web-grounded Microsoft Copilot instead of tenant-grounded Copilot.

questions.stem:
Your company is deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot. Early pilot results show inconsistent usage across departments.

You need to create a network of internal advocates to promote effective and responsible use.

What is the best approach to achieve the goal?

options.text: Rotate advocacy responsibilities among employees each quarter.
Encourage voluntary participation without assigning clear responsibilities.
Require all guidance and communication to come only from the IT department.
Establish defined expectations, such as peer enablement, feedback collection, and sharing practical use cases.

questions.stem:
Your company is deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Security leaders are concerned about prompt injection attacks embedded in external documents.

What is the most important control to reduce this risk?

options.text: enforcing least-privilege access and data protection policies
increasing the maximum token limit for Copilot responses
limiting Copilot responses to shorter summaries
training users to write more detailed prompts

questions.stem:
You are deploying Microsoft 365 Copilot and a Copilot Studio agent that answers HR policy questions. The agent retrieves contentfrom Microsoft SharePoint Online sites that contain GDPR-regulated personal data.

Leadership is concerned that responses might surface content from SharePoint sites where permissions are overly broad.

You need to resolve this concern for the current agent and all future agents.

What should you do?

options.text: Modify the SharePoint permissions to enforce least-privilege access.
Disable connected experiences that analyze the content in Microsoft 365 Apps.
Use Copilot content filtering to prevent all sensitive data from appearing in responses.
Enable all agents in integrated apps and require users to enable the agent only when needed.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework?

options.text: Enables companies to create operating system-level Copilot integrations.
Enables companies to build fully custom Al solutions by using Azure OpenAl.
Enables companies to customize visual themes and branding in Copilot experiences.
Enables companies to surface external data and services into Copilot by using connectors and plugins.

questions.stem:
You are evaluating the operational costs of deploying a generative Al solution at scale.

Which two factors directly influence usage-based costs? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: the number of tokens processed in prompts and responses
the number of users interacting with the solution
the selected model and its pricing tier
the total number of internal policies documented
the volume of historical data stored in databases

questions.stem: Your organization is deploying an internal assistant that answers HR policy questions grounded in SharePoint content.   The AI council asks how you will prevent an employee from receiving an answer drawn from a document they are not permitted to open.   Which control addresses this requirement?

options.text: Apply a content safety filter to the assistant's outputs.
Enforce Microsoft Entra authentication and role-based access control so retrieval returns only content the signed-in user can already access.
Lower the model temperature so responses are more deterministic.
Expand the grounding index so more documents are available to the assistant.

questions.stem: A customer-facing agent built on Microsoft Foundry can call an internal pricing tool.  During a security review the team is asked how it will stop a crafted user message from making the agent misuse that tool.   Which security category does this concern belong to, and what is the appropriate mitigation?

options.text: Data security; encrypt the pricing database at rest.
Authentication; require multifactor authentication for every user of the agent.
Application security; add prompt injection defences and restrict the agent to an approved tool allow-list.
Data residency; deploy the model in the same region as the pricing database.

questions.stem: Leadership wants assurance that confidential documents summarized by an AI assistant keep their protection when the summary is saved as a new file and shared.   Which control set should you cite?

options.text: Sensitivity labels enforced at retrieval and inherited by generated outputs, with data loss prevention applied to sharing.
A larger context window so the entire document fits in a single prompt.
Fine-tuning the model on the confidential document set.
Moving the documents to a single open location so retrieval is simpler.

questions.stem: AI pilots are running in six departments with no shared rules.   The CIO wants a single body that sets strategy, approves high-impact use cases, and keeps legal, security, HR and the business aligned.   What should the organization establish?

options.text: An AI champions program
An adoption team.
An AI council.
A data engineering center of excellence.

questions.stem: Your executive team asks whether appointing a single Chief AI Ethics Officer is sufficient to satisfy governance expectations for the AI programme.   What is the best response?

options.text: Yes, provided the officer reports directly to the board.
No. Governance rests on published principles and a cross-functional AI council; a single officer is one optional way to implement them.
Yes. A single accountable officer is the required governance model for AI.
No. Governance should be delegated entirely to each business unit.

questions.stem: The AI council has approved the first wave of Microsoft 365 Copilot.   Someone must now own the wave plan, communications, training, licence assignment and adoption reporting.   Which structure owns this work?

options.text: The AI council.
The adoption team.
The AI champions program.
The security operations centre.

questions.stem: Six weeks into a Copilot rollout, licensed users are active but shallow: most only summarize email.   Interviews show that people do not know what else to try and do not trust the output for client-facing work.   Which barriers are you facing, and what is the most appropriate first countermeasure? More than one answer choice may achieve the goal. Select the BEST answer.

options.text: Cost uncertainty and licensing; move the population to pay-as-you-go.
A skills gap and a trust concern; run role-based enablement through a champions program and teach grounding and citation checking.
Data readiness and oversharing; start a permissions remediation project.
Weak executive sponsorship; escalate to the board for a mandate.

questions.stem: You need peer-level support for adoption across 40 teams without adding headcount.   Which motion should you establish, and how should members be chosen?

options.text: An AI council, made up of the most senior leader in each team.
An adoption team, staffed with one IT administrator per region.
An AI champions program, selecting people for influence and enthusiasm rather than seniority and enabling them ahead of their peers.
A vendor-led help desk staffed by external contractors.

questions.stem: Frontline staff have Microsoft 365 but no Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.   They need a safe AI chat tool they can use from a phone and from the web, where they can upload a PDF and ask questions about it, and where prompts are not used to train foundation models.   What should you tell them they can use today?

options.text: Nothing until Microsoft 365 Copilot licences are purchased.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, which offers secure AI chat with enterprise data protection, file upload and mobile access.
A Copilot Studio agent published to a public website.
Microsoft Foundry, deployed to each user's device.

questions.stem: A director asks Copilot to summarise everything her team discussed about a customer across last month's meetings, chats and documents, and gets an incomplete answer.   She is using Copilot Chat without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.   What is the correct explanation?

options.text: Copilot Chat is web-grounded and does not provide broad grounding across her Microsoft 365 content; that requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
Copilot Chat cannot process natural language questions of that length.
Microsoft Graph does not index meetings, chats or documents.
The tenant has not enabled pay-as-you-go agents.

questions.stem: Your service desk runs on a third-party ticketing platform.   Leadership wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to answer questions using those tickets while preserving who is allowed to see what.   Which element of the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework applies?

options.text: Connectors, which bring external content into the Copilot grounding surface with permissions preserved.
The Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs, which embed Copilot into third-party applications.
Fine-tuning a model on an export of the ticket history.
Building a standalone application on Microsoft Foundry.

questions.stem: Which set correctly lists the components of the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework?

options.text: Agents, connectors, the Work IQ API, and the Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs.
Copilot Chat, Researcher, Analyst, and Copilot Pages.
Azure AI Search, Document Intelligence, Vision, and Language.
Pay-as-you-go, monthly subscription, and included licensing.

questions.stem: A strategy lead must produce a twelve-page briefing on entering a new market, drawing on internal planning documents and public sources, with every claim traceable to a citation.   Which Microsoft 365 Copilot capability should she use?

options.text: Analyst, because the briefing will include figures.
Researcher, because the task is multi-step research across work and web content producing cited synthesis.
Copilot in PowerPoint, because the output is a leadership deliverable.
A Copilot Studio agent, because the task recurs quarterly

questions.stem: A finance manager has three years of monthly revenue in a workbook and needs a seasonality-adjusted forecast for the next four quarters with a chart, and she does not write code.   Which capability should she use?

options.text: Researcher, because forecasting requires external market context.
Analyst, because the task is advanced data analysis with Python-backed reasoning and visualization.
Copilot Chat, because the workbook can be uploaded.
Azure AI Search, because the data must first be indexed.

questions.stem: A customer-service quality model performs well overall but consistently misjudges cases from two of your eight operating regions.   Reviewing the training data shows 92 percent of it came from the two largest regions.   What is the most accurate description of the problem, and the correct first fix?

options.text: Poor data quality; run a de-duplication and cleansing pass.
An unrepresentative dataset; collect and include data that reflects all eight regions before retraining.
Insufficient data volume; add more records from the two largest regions.
A prompt engineering problem; add regional context to the prompt.

questions.stem: A regulated insurer needs an AI solution that applies its own underwriting rules, runs inside its own application, and must be evaluated and audited against internal model risk policy.   Which approach fits, and why?

options.text: Buy, because Microsoft 365 Copilot already summarises documents.
Extend, because a connector can bring underwriting data into Copilot.
Build on Microsoft Foundry, because the solution needs its own model, tool and agent lifecycle with evaluation and observability.
Build a Copilot Studio agent, because it is low-code.

questions.stem: A solution architect explains that Microsoft 365 Copilot relies on two components: one that supplies work data and enforces permissions, and one that adds context about how work gets done.   Which statement correctly describes Work IQ?

options.text: Work IQ replaces Microsoft Graph as the data layer for Microsoft 365 content.
Work IQ is the intelligence layer built on Microsoft Graph that understands context, work patterns and relevance.
Work IQ is the licensing model that meters agent consumption in Copilot Chat.
Work IQ is the content safety service that filters harmful Copilot responses.

questions.stem: Your company is moving a Foundry Tools workload from pilot into production. Volume is now steady and predictable month to month, and finance wants the lowest unit cost with a forecastable monthly bill.   Which subscription model should you recommend?

options.text: Pay-as-you-go, because it requires no upfront commitment.
A commitment tier, because pre-paid reserved capacity gives a discounted unit rate and predictable monthly cost for steady volume.
A per-user monthly Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription.
Enterprise data protection, because it reduces token consumption.

questions.stem: Tailwind Traders wants an agent to answer questions grounded across several enterprise repositories, and requires that each user sees only what they are already permitted to open, without the team assembling and maintaining a retrieval pipeline.   Which capability should you recommend?

options.text: Fine-tune a model on an export of all repositories.
Foundry IQ, the managed, permission-aware knowledge layer for grounding agents.
Increase the model's context window and paste the documents into each prompt.
Copilot Pages, so answers can be shared across the team.

questions.stem: A manager asks why Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is considered safe for business use when consumer chat assistants are not approved.   Which characteristic should you cite?

options.text: It runs entirely offline on the user's device.
Enterprise data protection, meaning prompts, responses and tenant content are not used to train foundation models and stay inside the organization's compliance boundary.
It cannot access the web, so no external content is ever returned.
It requires a per-user Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for every user.

questions.stem: You are briefing leaders on secure AI for an upcoming deployment.   Which two areas does the assessment expect a leader to evaluate alongside data security? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.   Select TWO answers.

options.text: application security, including prompt injection defences and an approved tool allow-list
model temperature and top-p sampling settings
authentication requirements, including Microsoft Entra identity and role-based access control
the number of tokens consumed per user each month
the choice between supervised and unsupervised learning

questions.stem: Your organization is preparing a data readiness review before funding a grounded AI assistant.   Which two properties of the data should the review assess in addition to data quality? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.   Select TWO answers.

options.text: data type, because structured, unstructured and media content determine which AI capability applies
the physical storage medium used by the data centre
whether the dataset is representative of every population, region and edge case the solution will serve
the programming language used to build the retrieval pipeline
the number of employees who will use the assistant

questions.stem:
You are using a generative Al solution to draft executive summaries from internal reports. The responses are often too generic andare irrelevant to the organization.

Which prompt engineering technique should you use to improve the quality of the responses?

options.text: Increase the maximum response length.
Request multiple variations of the same summary in one prompt.
Assign a creative writing tone to make the summaries more engaging.
Provide clear instructions and include specific business context in the prompt.

questions.stem:
A retail company receives many open-ended customer questions about products and policies.

The company needs a solution to help them quickly draft friendly and accurate replies based on their internal data.

Which approach best achieves the goal? More than one answer choice may achieve the goal. 

Select the BEST answer.

options.text: a generative Al agent grounded in the company's product and policy data
a machine learning classification model that labels customer inquiries by category
a rules-based decision tree that routes inquiries to predefined FAQ responses
a traditional analytics dashboard that displays customer inquiry trends

questions.stem:
A business team is evaluating whether to use a generative Al solution or a rules-based automation system.

You need to identify a key characteristic of generative Al.

Which characteristic distinguishes generative Al from a rules-based system?

options.text: A rules-based system requires manually defined logic for every possible scenario.
A rules-based system follows predefined decision paths to produce consistent outputs.
A rules-based system produces the same output each time for a given structured input.
Generative Al generates responses by learning patterns from large datasets rather than relying on predefined rules.

questions.stem:
A team deploys a generative Al assistant to summarize regulatory documents.

During testing, the assistant occasionally includes statements that are NOT supported by the source material.

Which challenge of generative Al is this an example of?

options.text: automation bias
fabrication of information
overfitting to training data
scalability limitations

questions.stem:
A company is deciding whether to use a pretrained model or a fine-tuned model.

What is a key characteristic of a fine-tuned model compared to a pretrained model?

options.text: A pretrained model must always be trained from scratch before it can be used.
A pretrained model is trained only on an organization's internal proprietary data.
A fine-tuned model requires no training data and generates responses by using rules-based logic.
A fine-tuned model is adapted with additional domain-specific data to improve performance for a targeted task.

questions.stem:
A company deploys generative Al to draft internal knowledge base articles.

During testing, the generative Al system produces clear and accurate drafts in some test cases and incomplete or inconsistent drafts for similar inputs during other tests.

Which challenge of generative Al is this an example of?

options.text: bias
fabrication
reliability
scalability

questions.stem:
A company wants to automatically draft marketing emails based on customer input and product data.

Which type of model is required?

options.text: a generative Al model that produces new content
a predictive model that forecasts customer behavior
a statistical model that classifies customer segments
a rules-based system that follows predefined decision logic

questions.stem:
Your company wants to reduce equipment downtime in its manufacturing plants. The company collects operational readings andmaintenance records over time.

You need to recommend a solution that predicts equipment failures before they occur.

What should you recommend?

options.text: a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) solution
a prompt engineering framework for maintenance staff
a generative Al solution that summarizes maintenance logs
a machine learning model trained on historical sensor data

questions.stem:
You are leading the rollout of a machine learning solution. The model is already deployed to production.

You need to ensure that the solution continues to deliver accurate results as customer behavior changes.

What activity should you prioritize?

options.text: continuously monitoring model performance and retraining the model as needed
defining marketing campaign messaging to align with predicted churn segments
expanding the number of users that can access the model outputs
increasing the size of the original training dataset without evaluating model performance

questions.stem:
Your company is deploying a domain-specific Al agent to review legal contracts.

Early testing with a pretrained large language model (LLM) produces inconsistent terminology and formatting, even when using detailed prompts.

You are considering whether to fine-tune the model.

Which statement best describes how fine-tuning differs from using the pretrained model as is?

More than one answer choice may achieve the goal. Select the BEST answer.

options.text: Fine-tuning requires only modifying prompt instructions during inference without retraining the model.
Fine-tuning replaces the pretrained model by training a completely new model from scratch on a large dataset.
Fine-tuning limits responses to information retrieved from enterprise documents at query time without changing the model.
Fine-tuning adjusts the model's weights by training it on a smaller, domain-specific dataset to improve performance for targeted tasks.

questions.stem:
Your company has an internal support portal that uses a large language model (LLM)-based agent to answer employee policy questions. Policy documents are stored in Microsoft SharePoint Online and updated weekly, and responses must cite the exact source and reflect updates within 24 hours.

The agent sometimes generates responses that are NOT in the approved policy documents.

You need to ensure that responses are grounded in the latest approved content and include verifiable citations.

What should you do?

options.text: Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
Increase the model temperature to generate more diverse responses.
Use a web-grounded chat experience to search public internet sources.
Fine-tune a generative Al model on the SharePoint policy documents every week.

questions.stem:
Your company is evaluating Al technologies to improve operations.

A business leader asks how generative Al differs from traditional predictive Al systems.

Which statement most accurately describes generative Al?

options.text: Generative Al detects anomalies in datasets by identifying statistical deviations.
Generative Al classifies input data into predefined categories based on labeled training data.
Generative Al analyzes historical data to predict future outcomes without creating new content.
Generative Al creates new content, such as text, images, and code, based on patterns learned from data.

questions.stem:
Select the answer that correctly completes the sentence.

For Generative AI Models, supervised fine-tuning is used to adapt a [XXXXXXXXX] by training it on labeled input-output pairs for specific tasks and organizational requirements.

options.text: grounding source
pretrained model
prompt template
tokenized dataset

questions.stem:
You are using a generative Al solution to create policy summaries for employees across multiple departments. Some responses include fabricated details that are NOT in the source material.

Which prompt engineering technique should you use to reduce the likelihood of fabricated content?

options.text: Use more formal language when writing the prompt.
Request that the model generate multiple summary variations.
Ask the model to provide the most detailed response possible.
Instruct the model to base its response only on the provided source content.

questions.stem:
You are developing a GPT model in Microsoft Foundry to generate detailed financial reports. The reports require the analysis of multiple complex data inputs to produce structured written summaries.

Which type of model should you use?

options.text: large language model (LLM)
Diffusion Model
speech-to-text model
vision model

questions.stem: Your company plans to use Copilot to reference data from an external CRM system, while continuing to respect existing Microsoft 365 permissions. You need to make the CRM data available for data grounding. Which should you use?

options.text: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors
Microsoft Copilot Studio
Microsoft Graph Explorer

questions.stem: You are leading the deployment of an AI solution that generates customer-facing product recommendations. Executive leadership requires that your AI governance framework align with Microsoft responsible AI principles. You need to establish governance controls that reduce the risk of biased outputs and ensure that customers understand how AI is being used. Which two principles should you prioritize? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Accountability
Fairness
Reliability
Safety
Transparency

questions.stem: You are sponsoring an AI solution that will automate eligibility assessments for a financial assistance program. The solution will directly influence decisions that affect customers. You need to ensure the AI solution meets he Microsoft Responsible AI Standard for consistent performance and organizational oversight. Which two principles should you prioritize? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Accessibility
Accountability
Fairness
Reliability and safety
Scalability

questions.stem: Your company plans to deploy AI solutions that extract structured data from documents and enable natural language search across internal knowledge. Which two Microsoft Foundry capabilities should you recommend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Azure AI Search
Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools
Model fine-tuning
Prompt flow
Speech to text in Azure Speech

questions.stem:
You are evaluating Microsoft Foundry for building enterprise AI solutions.
Which two security capabilities are supported by using Foundry? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Public sharing of model outputs across tenants
Unrestricted anonymous access to deployed models
Training foundation models by using shared customer data
The isolation of customer data within the tenant boundary
Integration with Microsoft Entra ID for role-based access control (RBAC)

questions.stem: You are deploying an AI service that generates personalized product recommendations based on customer purchase history. You need to explain why to apply responsible AI principles before deployment. Which two explanations should you provide? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Removes the need for ongoing human oversight
Supports transparency in customer data usage
Increases automation that removes governance controls
Shifts compliance responsibility entirely to Microsoft
Prevents biased recommendations that can harm customer trust

questions.stem: Your company is planning a large-scale rollout of an Azure AI service for a production workload that has stable and predictable monthly usage. The finance department requires consistent monthly spending and minimal billing variability. You need to select the most appropriate subscription model. What should you choose?

options.text: Per-user Microsoft 365 licensing
Pay-as-you-go consumption billing
A separate Azure subscription for each department
A prepaid capacity commitment for the Azure AI service

questions.stem: Employees need to search internal content by using natural language, find conceptually related information, and limit results to specific document categories. Which Azure AI Search capability supports this requirement?

options.text: AI enrichment
Hybrid search
Semantic ranking
Skillset indexing

questions.stem: Your company plans to deploy an Azure AI solution trained on historical customer data. During a review, you discover that most of the training data comes from a single customer segment, while other segments are underrepresented. You need to assess the potential impact before deployment. What is the primary risk?

options.text: The model will become unsupervised because the dataset is incomplete.
The AI solution will require fewer compute resources during inference.
The AI solution will rebalance predictions automatically over time without additional data.
The AI solution might generate responses that do not generalize well across all customer segments.

questions.stem: Select the answer that correctly completes the sentence. When a company needs to extract structured data, such as contract terms and renewal dates, from large volumes of documents, it should use _______.

options.text: Azure AI Search
Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools
Azure Vision in Foundry Tools
Prompt flow in Microsoft Foundry

questions.stem: You need to explain the value of Microsoft Foundry to stakeholders. Which statement accurately describes a key benefit of Foundry?

options.text: Provides tools for automating business process with AI, without requiring AI models.
Supports building custom AI models by using open-source development frameworks only.
Focuses primarily on delivering AI capabilities within Microsoft 365 productivity apps.
Enables the centralized management and governance of AI solutions across an organization.

questions.stem: Your company plans to use Microsoft Foundry to build generative AI solutions that process sensitive internal data across multiple departments.Which benefit of Foundry supports this requirement?

options.text: Model outputs are shared across organizations to enhance collaboration.
Enterprise data remains within the company's tenant boundary during model use.
User access to AI solutions is managed independently by each application team.
Foundation models are retrained by using aggregated customer data to improve accuracy.

questions.stem: You are evaluating Microsoft Foundry for enterprise generative AI initiatives. Which two benefits of Foundry should you highlight to stakeholders? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Access to foundation models from multiple providers in a single environment
The ability to scale AI deployments across regions and business units
The automatic replacement of legacy business applications
The need to train custom models for every solution
Use of public shared datasets for enterprise model training

questions.stem: Your company is developing an AI solution to summarize customer feedback. The training data consists primarily of feedback from one geographic region, even though the company operates globally. After deploying the solution, users report that summaries do NOT reflect concerns from other regions. What is the primary cause of the issue?

options.text: The model requires a larger token limit.
The model lacks sufficient prompt engineering guidance.
The solution uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
The training data fails to represent the full customer base.

questions.stem: Your company plans to pilot Microsoft Copilot Studio for customer support and deploy a protected partner model from Microsoft Foundry Models by using the same Azure subscription. During deployment, you receive a notification that the subscription is NOT authorized for partner model purchases. You need both initiatives to use pay-as-you-go billing with the existing Azure subscription without changing billing models. What should you do?

options.text: Switch the model deployment to prepaid Azure capacity.
Create a new Azure subscription dedicated to AI workloads.
Enable Azure Marketplace purchases for the existing Azure subscription.
Purchase Copilot Studio message packs instead of pay-as-you-go billing.

questions.stem: Your company is preparing to expand Microsoft 365 Copilot beyond a small pilot group. Leadership has decided to form a centralized team to guide governance, rollout planning, and risk management across departments. What is the best approach to ensure that the team operates effectively? More than one answer choice may achieve the goal. Select the BEST answer.

options.text: Assign an executive sponsor to oversee the rollout.
Rotate rollout responsibilities between departments each quarter.
Define clear decision-making authority and accountability for the team.
Enable each department to manage its own rollout timeline and governance approach.
